newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Losses of South Korea listed companies widen.
newsitem.headline: Losses of South Korea listed companies widen.

text.p: Net losses of 16 South Korean listed companies whose financial year ends in September surged by 232 percent in the first half, the Securities Supervisory Board (SSB) said on Friday.
October-March losses of the companies totalled 25.85 billion won against a deficit of 7.78 billion a year earlier.

Combined recurring losses reached 12.65 billion won against recurring profit of 1.2 billion won. Recurring profits, usually before-tax, are total revenues minus total costs. Net profits, mostly after-tax, take into account extraordinaries.
Sales of the 16 companies in the six-month period totalled 1.36 trillion won, up from 1.18 trillion a year ago, an increase of 15.9 percent.
The SSB said assets of those companies were valued at 4.17 trillion won at the end of March, up 12.63 percent from a year earlier. Their combined debts rose 21.23 percent to 3.16 trillion won.
In all, 17 listed companies report earnings based on a fiscal year ending in September. One is currently in court receivership.
Most listed companies report earnings on a calendar year.
